paper_title: Mechanistic Understanding and Mitigation of Language Confusion in   English-Centric Large Language Models
caption: Distribution of Important Neurons Associated with Confusion Points in Llama3-8B. (a) Distribution of the top 300 most important FFN neurons across layers for an individual Chinese prompt “UTF8gbsn请解释拆东墙补西墙的意思。(Please explain `UTF8gbsn拆东墙补西墙.')” from Aya. (b) Aggregated distribution of important neuron scores across all Chinese test samples in Aya.

model_annotations.English:
Both plots illustrate the distribution of neuron activity across layers in the Llama3-8B model. The x-axis for both plots represents “layer”, with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 35, and tick labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis represents “count”, with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 175 for plot (b) and 0 to 100 for plot (a), with tick labels at intervals of 25 and 10 respectively. 

Plot (a) displays a single blue line with circular markers representing the count of FFN value neurons for an individual case. Starting at a count of approximately 2 when layer equals 0, the line remains relatively stable around a count of 5 to 15 until layer 20. From layer 20 to 25, the count increases steeply to approximately 68, and then decreases to 43 when layer equals 30. 

Plot (b) displays a single green line with circular markers representing the aggregated neuron scores. Beginning at a count of approximately 1 when layer is 0, the line remains largely constant around a count of 5, until layer 30, when it increases sharply to a value of approximately 155.
model_annotations.German:
Both plots share a common x-axis labeled “layer”, with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 32, and tick labels at integer intervals. They also share a common y-axis labeled “count”, with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 175 and tick labels at integer intervals. 

Plot (a), titled “Individual Case”, illustrates the count of Llama3 FFN value neurons across different layers. This is represented by a blue line with circular markers and a solid style. Starting at a value of approximately 1 at layer 0, the line remains relatively flat, fluctuating between 1 and 4 until layer 20. At layer 20, the count increases to a value of 12, and then rises sharply to a peak of 95 at layer 32. 

Plot (b), titled “Aggregated Neuron Scores”, illustrates the count of Llama3 FFN value neurons across different layers. This is represented by a green line with circular markers and a solid style. The line begins at a value of approximately 4 at layer 0 and remains relatively stable, fluctuating between 4 and 6 until layer 25. At layer 25, the count increases to a value of 22, and increases again to a value of 145 at layer 32.
